transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Jonas Patel - Redwood; Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao, Evan Morales - Galene Systems

Summary (auto): quick readout of last week's bench, focus on p95 tail and throughput deltas vs BlueForge; discuss dedicated-slot run for peak sim; agree on artifacts to share.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, agenda is bench readout, tuning notes, and next steps. Jonas is gonna walk through the telemetry we pulled.
[00:18] Jonas Patel: cool, thanks Maya. quick preface — the numbers i'm about to read are from our lab with your model payloads that Priya shared, batch size 4, seq len 512, KV cache warm enabled for the prefix cases.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: right, that's the same config we used against BlueForge last month, so should be apples-to-apples mostly.
[00:45] Jonas Patel: ok p50 latency on Redwood to generation token was 85ms, p95 was 320ms. Baseline, BlueForge, with same payloads showed p50 ~180ms and p95 ~950ms on their reported runs. throughput sustained at 130 req/s on our config vs their ~95 req/s.
[01:12] Priya Rao: those p95 numbers are a lot better, Jonas, is that with quantized weights?
[01:18] Jonas Patel: yes - we ran two modes: FP16 baseline and an int8-ish quant profile (we call it q4_1 in the runbook). The int8 profile shaved about 12-15% latency on median and 22% unit-cost savings overall. we also saw KV cache warm hits reduced p50 by another 10-12% for multi-turns.
[01:45] Evan Morales: can you clarify unit costs? we need to show CFO the delta.
[01:50] Maya Chen: sure, high level numbers from the pilot: Redwood unit cost estimate (incl compute amortized) ~ $8.50 per 1M tokens for your workload after quantization and caching, BlueForge estimate at same config was ~ $12.70 per 1M tokens. that's roughly a 33% reduction. Jonas, the detailed sheet has per-run breakdown.
[02:10] Jonas Patel: yep i'll attach the raw telemetry. also note that our routing policy tests showed when you enable fallback to a smaller variant during spikes we maintain p95 under 600ms, which keeps user-facing latency acceptable while preserving throughput. BlueForge fallback was more of a cold-switch with higher tail.
[02:35] Priya Rao: interesting. two operational Qs: 1) cold start behavior for new prefix caches, and 2) how burst autoscale affects downstream token limits we have in our app.
[02:45] Jonas Patel: cold start — on first warmup you'll see a 1-2 second hit for very large KV sets but that's amortized after a few requests; we recommend a short synthetic warm-run during deployments. For autoscale bursts we tested burst slots (dedicated burst capacity) — that keeps token rate increases smooth, but it does change unit cost during the burst windows.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: what's the recommended pattern if we want to keep costs predictable?
[03:14] Maya Chen: two levers: 1) use dedicated reserved slots for expected steady peak windows (monthly commit), 2) enable prefix caching + quantization for the heavy flows. combined they reduce unit cost variance. also routing to a slightly smaller model for non-critical branches cuts cost without user impact.
[03:35] Evan Morales: procurement will also ask about compliance — SOC2 / SSO / KMS. can you send the security pack?
[03:40] Maya Chen: yes — we'll send the security pack and a pointer to our SOC 2 report. Jonas, will you include KMS integration notes?
[03:46] Jonas Patel: will do, i'll add the note about customer-managed KMS for the Private deployment path and the audit log formats.
[03:52] Priya Rao: another datapoint — on Tuesday we hit a 20% higher burst than we simulated, some requests timed out at BlueForge and retried. do you have retry behavior details?
[04:00] Jonas Patel: by default we implement exponential backoff on the client side, and server side we have graceful queueing for short bursts. if you need very low retry exposure we recommend the dedicated slot or routing to a cheaper variant as a fallback.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: what's the friction to get a short dedicated slot test? we want to run with our traffic for 4 hours to validate.
[04:23] Maya Chen: low - we can provision a 4-hour reserved slot in lab, need Priya's traffic trace and Jonas will coordinate the orchestration.
[04:30] Jonas Patel: I'll prepare the runbook — it includes warmup steps, expected metrics to capture (p50/p95, tail tokens/sec, GPU utl), and post-run artifact locations.
[04:40] Priya Rao: we'll upload the 1hr peak capture by Friday. also please include the telemetry schema so we can compare automatically.
[04:48] Jonas Patel: noted. schema and ingestion script included in the sheet.
[04:55] Evan Morales: quick question on model parity — are there any differences in generation quality after quant? noise or hallucination shifts?
[05:02] Jonas Patel: we ran automated evals on your held-out prompts — minor score drift within 0.6% BLEU-like metric we use internally, and human spot checks saw negligible quality delta for the q4_1 profile. we'll include the eval set and diffs in the spreadsheet.
[05:20] Maya Chen: ok to recap — Redwood shows materially better median and tail vs BlueForge on your payloads, throughput is higher, and quantization + cache provide cost headroom. immediate next step is the 4-hour dedicated slot run to validate under your peak, security docs to be shared, and scheduling the compliance deep-dive.
[05:40] Priya Rao: sounds good. one more ask: can you annotate the runbook with the exact versions of kernels and runtime used? we've had infra teams ask for exact pinning.
[05:48] Jonas Patel: yes — i'll include kernel version, runtime digest, and the exact model artifact hash used in the tests.
[05:55] Liam O'Connor: great, thanks everyone.
[05:57] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the doc and set the next meeting.

Meeting end.

Artifacts referenced:
- bench_spreadsheet_galene_v3.csv (will be shared)
- dedicated_slot_runbook_v2.md (attached after call)
- security_pack_link (SOC2, KMS notes)
